messages.subject: R2 priors + Stan meetings
parts:
Ben --- is there a writeup somewhere on the (your?) R2 prior?
Or would you mind going over it at a Stan meeting some
time? Or out-of-meeting if not everyone's interested.

I'm really thinking our meetings are too big and rarely
are topics of general interest.

- Bob

messages.author: f53f4ca2c430170d
messages.subject: Re: R2 priors + Stan meetings
parts: On Tuesday, February 23, 2016 at 4:11:08 PM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:

> Ben --- is there a writeup somewhere on the (your?) R2 prior?
> Or would you mind going over it at a Stan meeting some
> time? Or out-of-meeting if not everyone's interested.
>
> I'm really thinking our meetings are too big and rarely
> are topics of general interest.

What's the point of the meetings supposed to be?

A lot of development discussion seems to happen in github issues and on this list (and that's great, really) but there are some things that just work better in person. As someone who is not at Columbia it's helpful for me to hear what different people are addressing because it provides some context for what I do... especially since I've been off in protobuf/io land for a while now... but if you are at Columbia you probably hear about it anyway.

I don't really mind the inefficiency in the current format because participating over Hangouts is low commitment but I would support some attempt at more focused discussion (do we need an agenda here?...)

Krzysztof

>
> - Bob

messages.author: 49e107cb0f8a3d27
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] R2 priors + Stan meetings
parts:
I was going to suggest that we discuss again the idea of separate Stan meetings for research and engineering. But then I realized that we’re already sort of doing this.

The weekly Stan meetings tend to be about engineering now, which is fine. The research ideas are discussed on various days that there’s something worth talking about, and among an inner circle of the developers that are interested in the topic too. Same goes for consulting. And when the research ideas start to be implemented in Stan, the discussion now becomes part of the weekly Stan meetings.

I like this set up. I also wish we do more reading groups!

Dustin
